title: Optimal-constant iff-split for Putnam 2025 A2
intent: Reduce the optimal-constant answer for Putnam 2025 A2 — that 1/π is the greatest lower bound and 4/π² the least upper bound of the constants sandwiching sin x between quadratic lower and upper bounds on [0, π] — to two order-antisymmetry splits, each of which is itself a conjunction of membership (the inequality holds) and optimality (every competing constant is worse). Each of the four halves is discharged by one already-proved named lemma.

parent.name: putnam_2025_a2
parent.statement:
theorem putnam_2025_a2 :
  IsGreatest {a : ℝ | ∀ x ∈ Icc 0 π, a * x * (π - x) ≤ sin x} (1 / π) ∧
  IsLeast {b : ℝ | ∀ x ∈ Icc 0 π, b * x * (π - x) ≥ sin x} (4 / π ^ 2) := by

children.name: sin_ge_inv_pi_mul_quad
children.statement: lemma sin_ge_inv_pi_mul_quad : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) π, (1 / π) * x * (π - x) ≤ sin x := by
children.closed_by: a case tree over x = 0, x = π, x ≤ π/2, x ≥ π - 2, x ≤ 1 (and the symmetric halves for x > π/2 via sin_pi_sub); each leaf closed by nlinarith/linarith, using sin_bound, mul_le_sin, sin_one_lower and sin_pi_sub

children.name: inv_pi_is_greatest_lower_bound
children.statement:
lemma inv_pi_is_greatest_lower_bound (a : ℝ) (h : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) π, a * x * (π - x) ≤ sin x) :
    a ≤ 1 / π := by
children.closed_by: by_contra; set x := min (min ((a - 1/π) / (2 * a)) (1/2)) (π/2); applying h at that x contradicts sin x ≤ x, closed by nlinarith

children.name: sin_le_four_div_pi_sq_mul_quad
children.statement: lemma sin_le_four_div_pi_sq_mul_quad : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) π, sin x ≤ (4 / π ^ 2) * x * (π - x) := by
children.closed_by: a case tree over x = 0, x = π, x ≤ π/2, x ≤ 0.6, x ≤ π - π^2/4 (and the symmetric halves for x > π/2 via sin_pi_sub); each leaf closed by nlinarith/linarith, using sin_le, sin_pi_sub, sin_pi_div_two and cos_bound

children.name: four_div_pi_sq_is_least_upper_bound
children.statement:
lemma four_div_pi_sq_is_least_upper_bound (b : ℝ) (h : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0:ℝ) π, b * x * (π - x) ≥ sin x) :
    4 / π ^ 2 ≤ b := by
children.closed_by: specialises h at x = π/2; sin (π/2) = 1 gives b * (π/2) * (π/2) ≥ 1, then nlinarith [hpi2]

applicability.goal_shape: an optimal-constant claim IsGreatest S c ∧ IsLeast T d, where each IsGreatest/IsLeast unfolds to a conjunction of membership (an inequality over a parameter set) and optimality (every element of the set is ≤/≥ the constant)
applicability.use_when: the two halves of each constant (the inequality holds, and every competing constant is worse) are already proved as named lemmas, so the main theorem is assembled by constructor + exact with no further arithmetic
applicability.avoid_when: the membership inequality and the optimality argument are entangled or need a case analysis that cannot be shared across halves; only one direction holds; or either half is not yet isolated as a self-contained named lemma

claims.claim: Three constructor applications (lines 514, 515, 519) split the conjunction into four leaf goals, and each leaf is closed by exactly one of the four named lemmas — sin_ge_inv_pi_mul_quad, inv_pi_is_greatest_lower_bound, sin_le_four_div_pi_sq_mul_quad, four_div_pi_sq_is_least_upper_bound — in 9 lines (514-522).

metrics.how_counted: glue = lines 514-522 of the copied file; child proof bodies = lines 21-192, 197-250, 254-485, 490-509; depth = putnam_2025_a2 → sin_ge_inv_pi_mul_quad → sin_one_lower (sin_one_lower used at lines 127 and 188)

consequences: The move creates exactly four obligations — the four conjuncts — and no exhaustiveness obligation, because constructor on ∧ and on IsGreatest/IsLeast produces precisely the two halves of each conjunction. It relies on the four lemmas being already proved and in scope; if one is missing, that half becomes a sorry-able hole whose statement is exactly the leaf lemma. Failure mode: the membership and optimality halves are both inequalities about the same expression a * x * (π - x), so the wrong lemma can be supplied to the wrong half; the split shape is still right, but exact fails on the type of the constant.
